steps.text: These games can be played anytime during Book 2 (at the end of a lesson, or instead of a lesson if a student is tired). All of these games use words with three sounds and short vowels.
Bring out the blank tiles. Put out the correct number of tiles for the first word.
Tutor touches and says the first word, then touches and says each sound.
Student changes the first tile and creates the first rhyming word. Student says the sound of that first tile, then says the new word.
Tutor changes the second tile and creates the second rhyming word. Repeat this process for as long as possible.
Good 3-tile rhyming words to start with: FAN, RICH, PIT, DASH, MAD, BILL, LAP, DID, BIG, BUN.
Bring out the letter tiles the student has already learned. Build a CVC (Consonant-Vowel-Consonant) Real word.
Take turns changing just ONE tile to create a new word. Whoever gets stuck first loses.

Variation 1: You must make a NONSENSE word.
Variation 2: Put down just a beginning Consonant and Vowel. Take turns seeing how many real words you can create by changing just the LAST sound.
Build a trail out of letters written on index cards. (Only use letters the student has been taught).
Student pulls a picture from the draw pile, says the name of the picture, and says just its first sound.
Student matches the sound to the LETTER in the trail and moves their piece.
Write homonym pairs on index cards (e.g., by-buy, aunt-ant, be-bee, tail-tale, see-sea, right-write, two-too, cent-sent, hear-here).
I'm going to show you pairs of words that sound the same but mean different things. Do you know what these mean?
Play Concentration with the cards. When a match is found, offer bonus points if the student can use the word(s) in a sentence.
Write each letter and vowel learned on at least two index cards. Shuffle and place face down in rows.
Turn over one card and make its sound. Then turn over another card and make its sound.
If the turned-over cards make the same sound, the student keeps the pair. (Note: C and K cards would be considered a pair since they make the same sound).
Write each letter and vowel on at least four index cards. Deal 6 cards to each player.
Look at your hand. Ask me: 'Do you have a card that says /xxx/?'
If the opponent has a card that makes that sound, they hand it over. If not, say 'Go Fish' and the player draws from the deck.
Write each phrase your student has learned on an index card. Shuffle.
Have the student read the phrase and decide if it is a Who, Did What, or Where phrase.
Put a Red stripe for 'Who', Blue for 'Did What', and Green for 'Where'.
Build a sentence by putting down a red card, a blue card, and a green card. Have the student read it and tell you if it is real or silly.
Write real and nonsense words on index cards. Shuffle.
Have the student draw a card, read the word, and put it in a 'Real' pile or a 'Nonsense' pile.
To make it more competitive, set a 3-minute timer and count how many they can read accurately. Penalize inaccurate readings by taking away a point.
